newsitem.title: BELGIUM: NATO agrees to 18-month mission in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: NATO agrees to 18-month mission in Bosnia.

text.p: NATO ambassadors have agreed that a new Stabilisation Force (SFOR) in Bosnia would stay in the country for no more than 18 months, NATO sources said on Wednesday.

"There's basic agreement...that we will be planning for 18 months," one source at North Atlantic Treaty Organisation headquarters said, adding that the ambassadors would agree the plan formally later in the evening.
"That doesn't necessarily mean we will be staying for 18 months," the source said. "There will be reviews. Our aim is not to have any more troops there at any one time than is absolutely necessary."
NATO last week agreed to a plan for about 30,000 troops to stay on in Bosnia after the mandate of its Implemenation Force (IFOR) expires on Decemeber 20.
But the issue of how long the new SFOR mission would stay was still undecided. France had said two years may be needed, while Germany favoured one.
The United States, the most powerful nation in NATO, said it would keep its troops in Bosnia for 18 months, reviewing their presence every six months.
